units.title: Variables and Types
units.tip: Kotlin has two kinds of variables. A val is read-only: it cannot be reassigned once set. A var is mutable: it can be reassigned. Type inference means Kotlin figures out the type automatically from the assigned value, but you can also declare types explicitly.

exercises.question: What is the difference between val and var in Kotlin?
exercises.answer: val cannot be reassigned; var can be reassigned
exercises.explain: val stands for value: once it is set, it cannot be reassigned. var stands for variable and can be reassigned multiple times.
choices: val cannot be reassigned; var can be reassigned
val is for integers; var is for strings
val is faster; var is slower
val requires type declaration; var does not

exercises.question: Which declaration is valid in Kotlin?
exercises.answer: val name = "Alice"
exercises.explain: val creates a read-only variable that cannot be reassigned, so val name = "Alice" is valid. int x = 5 is Java syntax, not Kotlin, and val count = 5; count = 6 fails because a val cannot be reassigned.
choices: Both var and val can be reassigned

exercises.question: When should you use val instead of var?
exercises.answer: When the variable will not change after assignment
exercises.explain: Using val by default makes code safer and more predictable. Only use var when the value truly needs to change.
choices: When the variable stores a number
When the variable will not change after assignment

exercises.question: What happens if you try to reassign a val?
exercises.answer: Compilation error
exercises.explain: val variables are final and cannot be reassigned. The compiler catches this error before runtime.

exercises.question: A value is set once and never changes. Which declaration follows best practice?
exercises.answer: val age = 25
exercises.explain: Using val by default is Kotlin best practice. It makes your intent clear and prevents accidental reassignment, and var is only needed when the value really changes.

exercises.question: What does type inference mean in Kotlin?
exercises.answer: The compiler automatically determines variable types
exercises.explain: Kotlin infers the type from the assigned value, so you often do not need to specify Int, String, etc. explicitly.
choices: You must always declare types explicitly
The compiler automatically determines variable types
Variables have no type until runtime

exercises.question: In the line val x = 42, what is the inferred type of x?
exercises.answer: Int
exercises.explain: 42 is a whole number literal, so Kotlin infers x as type Int.

exercises.question: How do you explicitly declare a variable type in Kotlin?
exercises.answer: val name: String = "Alice"
exercises.explain: The type goes after the variable name, separated by a colon.

exercises.question: What is the inferred type of val pi = 3.14?
exercises.answer: Double
exercises.explain: A floating-point literal like 3.14 defaults to Double in Kotlin.

exercises.question: Which is valid Kotlin?
exercises.answer: val message: String = "Hello"
exercises.explain: This declares a val with an explicit String type and assigns a string value.

units.title: Null Safety
units.tip: Kotlin addresses null pointer exceptions by requiring you to explicitly mark nullable types with a question mark (?). The safe call operator (?.) and Elvis operator (?:) handle nulls gracefully, while the not-null assertion operator (!!), sometimes called the force operator, should only be used when you are certain a value exists.

exercises.question: How do you declare a nullable variable in Kotlin?
exercises.answer: val name: String? = null
exercises.explain: The question mark (?) marks a type as nullable, meaning it can hold null. Without ?, a variable cannot be null.

exercises.question: What is the difference between String and String? in Kotlin?
exercises.answer: String cannot be null; String? can be null
exercises.explain: String is a non-nullable type and always holds a value. String? is nullable and can hold null.
choices: String cannot be null; String? can be null

exercises.question: Can you assign null to a non-nullable variable?
exercises.answer: No, the compiler prevents it
exercises.explain: Non-nullable types cannot hold null. The compiler enforces this at compile time, which helps avoid null pointer exceptions.

exercises.question: What is the primary benefit of Kotlin's nullable types?
exercises.answer: Catching possible null pointer errors at compile time
exercises.explain: By marking types as nullable or non-nullable, Kotlin catches many potential null issues before the code runs.
choices: Catching possible null pointer errors at compile time

exercises.question: Which declaration is correct?
exercises.answer: val age: Int? = 25
exercises.explain: This declares a nullable Int and assigns a non-null value 25. This is valid; nullable types can hold non-null values.

exercises.question: What does the safe call operator (?.) do?
exercises.answer: Calls a method only if the object is not null
exercises.explain: The ?. operator calls a method or accesses a property only if the object is not null. If null, the expression returns null.
choices: Calls a method only if the object is not null

exercises.question: What is the Elvis operator (?:) used for?
exercises.answer: Providing a default value when the left side is null
exercises.explain: The ?: operator returns the left side if not null, otherwise the right side. It is useful for providing defaults.
choices: Providing a default value when the left side is null

exercises.question: What does val name = person.getName() ?: "Unknown" do?
exercises.answer: Calls getName(); if null, uses "Unknown"
exercises.explain: The Elvis operator ?: returns the left expression if not null, otherwise the right. This safely defaults to "Unknown" if getName() returns null.
choices: Throws an error if getName() is null

exercises.question: When should you use the force operator (!!)?
exercises.answer: Only when you are certain the value is not null
exercises.explain: !! asserts that a value is not null. Use it rarely; it throws an exception if the value is null.
choices: Instead of the safe call operator
Only when you are certain the value is not null

exercises.question: What happens if you use !! on a null value?
exercises.answer: Throws a NullPointerException
exercises.explain: The !! operator asserts non-null and crashes with NullPointerException if the value is actually null.

units.title: Functions and Lambdas
units.tip: Functions in Kotlin are declared with the fun keyword and can return values explicitly. Lambdas are shorthand anonymous functions, often passed as arguments. The last expression in a lambda is its return value.

exercises.question: How do you declare a function in Kotlin?
exercises.answer: fun greet(name: String): String { return "Hello, $name" }
exercises.explain: Functions start with fun, followed by the name, parameters in parentheses with types, the return type after a colon, and the body in braces.

exercises.question: What does a function parameter declaration like count: Int mean?
exercises.answer: The parameter count must be an Int
exercises.explain: In Kotlin, parameters require a type after a colon. count: Int means the parameter must be an integer.
choices: The parameter count must be an Int

exercises.question: How do you specify a function's return type?
exercises.answer: fun add(a: Int, b: Int): Int { return a + b }
exercises.explain: The return type goes after the parameter list, preceded by a colon. Here, the function returns an Int.
choices: fun add(a: Int, b: Int): Int { return a + b }
fun add(a: Int, b: Int) returns Int

exercises.question: In a function with a block body, how do you send a value back to the caller?
exercises.answer: Use the return keyword followed by the value
exercises.explain: In a function with a block body in braces, return sends a value back to the caller and ends the function.
choices: Assign the value to the function's name
Use the return keyword followed by the value

exercises.question: What is the return type of fun printMessage(msg: String) { println(msg) }?
exercises.answer: Unit
exercises.explain: Since no return type is declared, it defaults to Unit, which means the function returns no meaningful value.

exercises.question: What is a lambda in Kotlin?
exercises.answer: An anonymous function passed as a value
exercises.explain: Lambdas are shorthand anonymous functions enclosed in braces. They can be assigned to variables or passed as arguments.
choices: An anonymous function passed as a value

exercises.question: What is the syntax for a lambda that adds two numbers?
exercises.answer: { a, b -> a + b }
exercises.explain: Lambda syntax is { parameters -> expression }. The last expression is the return value.

exercises.question: In a lambda, what is the return value?
exercises.answer: The last expression
exercises.explain: Lambdas implicitly return the value of the last expression. No explicit return statement is needed.

exercises.question: If a function's last parameter is a lambda, where can you write the lambda?
exercises.answer: Outside the parentheses, in braces after the call
exercises.explain: Kotlin allows trailing lambda syntax: when the lambda is the last parameter, it can go in braces after the parentheses, as in list.map { it * 2 }. You can also pass it inside the parentheses.
choices: Outside the parentheses, in braces after the call
Lambdas cannot be passed as arguments

exercises.question: What does list.map { it * 2 } do?
exercises.answer: Returns a new list with each element doubled
exercises.explain: map applies the lambda { it * 2 } to each element. it is a shorthand for the current element.
choices: Returns a new list with each element doubled

units.title: Control Flow with When
units.tip: The when expression replaces switch statements and is more powerful. It can match exact values, ranges, types, or conditions. When you use it as an expression it returns a value, and it must cover every possible case, usually with an else branch.

exercises.question: What is the Kotlin equivalent of a switch statement?
exercises.answer: when expression
exercises.explain: when replaces switch and is more flexible and concise.

exercises.question: What does this code do? when (x) { 1 -> "one"; 2 -> "two"; else -> "other" }
exercises.answer: Returns "one" if x is 1, "two" if x is 2, otherwise "other"
exercises.explain: when checks the value of x against each branch and returns the matching string.
choices: Returns "one" if x is 1, "two" if x is 2, otherwise "other"

exercises.question: Is when a statement or an expression in Kotlin?
exercises.answer: An expression; it returns a value
exercises.explain: when is an expression, so it can be assigned to a variable or returned from a function.
choices: An expression; it returns a value
A loop that repeats until a branch matches

exercises.question: What does the else branch in when do?
exercises.answer: Handles any value not matched by other branches
exercises.explain: else matches anything not covered by the earlier branches. When when is used as an expression and its branches do not cover every possible value, an else branch is needed.
choices: Handles any value not matched by other branches

exercises.question: Can you assign the result of a when to a variable?
exercises.answer: Yes, val result = when (x) { ... }
exercises.explain: Since when is an expression, it returns a value that can be assigned to a variable.
choices: Only if x is an Int

exercises.question: How do you match a range in a when expression?
exercises.answer: in 1..10 -> "in range"
exercises.explain: The in operator checks if a value falls within a range.

exercises.question: What does when (x) { is String -> ... } do?
exercises.answer: Checks if x is a String type
exercises.explain: is checks the type of the value, allowing type-safe checking.
choices: Checks if x is a String type
Checks if x equals a string

exercises.question: Can you use multiple values in a single when branch?
exercises.answer: Yes, 1, 2, 3 -> "small"
exercises.explain: You can comma-separate multiple values to match any of them.

exercises.question: What is smart casting in when?
exercises.answer: After an is check, the variable is automatically treated as that type
exercises.explain: After checking is String, the variable is automatically treated as a String inside that branch, with no explicit cast needed.
choices: After an is check, the variable is automatically treated as that type

exercises.question: What does when (x) { else -> "default" } do?
exercises.answer: Always matches and returns "default"
exercises.explain: when with only an else branch always matches, effectively providing a single fallback.

units.title: Classes and Objects
units.tip: Classes define blueprints for objects. Kotlin allows properties and functions to be defined in a single, concise way. Data classes automatically generate equals(), hashCode(), toString(), and copy() methods, making them perfect for holding data.

exercises.question: How do you define a class in Kotlin?
exercises.answer: class Person { }
exercises.explain: Classes are declared with the class keyword, followed by a name and a body in braces.

exercises.question: Which declaration uses a primary constructor that also creates properties?
exercises.answer: class Person(val name: String, val age: Int) { }
exercises.explain: The primary constructor is defined in the class header. Parameters marked val or var automatically become class properties.
choices: class Person(val name: String, val age: Int) { }

exercises.question: What is the init block used for?
exercises.answer: Initialization code that runs when an object is created
exercises.explain: The init block executes when the object is instantiated, useful for initialization logic.
choices: Initialization code that runs when an object is created

exercises.question: How do you create an instance of a class?
exercises.answer: val person = Person("Alice", 25)
exercises.explain: Instantiate a class by calling its constructor without the new keyword.

exercises.question: Can you define functions inside a class?
exercises.answer: Yes, methods are functions defined in a class
exercises.explain: Classes contain both properties and functions (methods) that operate on the object's data.
choices: Yes, methods are functions defined in a class

exercises.question: What is a data class in Kotlin?
exercises.answer: A class that holds data and auto-generates utility methods
exercises.explain: Data classes automatically generate equals(), hashCode(), toString(), and copy() methods based on their properties.
choices: A class that only holds variables
A class that holds data and auto-generates utility methods
A class that cannot be instantiated

exercises.question: How do you declare a data class?
exercises.answer: data class Person(val name: String, val age: Int)
exercises.explain: Use the data keyword before class to make it a data class.
choices: data class Person(val name: String, val age: Int)

exercises.question: What does the copy() method do?
exercises.answer: Creates a new object with the same values, optionally changing some
exercises.explain: copy() returns a new instance with the same property values, and you can override chosen properties. The original object is not changed, which is useful for immutable updates.
choices: Changes the original object's properties in place
Creates a new object with the same values, optionally changing some

exercises.question: What does toString() do on a data class?
exercises.answer: Returns a string representation of the object
exercises.explain: Data classes auto-generate toString() to show property names and values in a readable format.
choices: Returns a string representation of the object

exercises.question: Which statement about data classes is true?
exercises.answer: Data classes must have at least one property
exercises.explain: The primary constructor of a data class needs at least one parameter, and each parameter must be marked val or var.
choices: Data classes must have at least one property
Data classes are slower than regular classes

units.title: Collections and Extension Functions
units.tip: Kotlin provides List, Set, and Map for storing multiple values. Extension functions let you add new methods to existing classes without inheritance. Many are built-in, like filter(), map(), and fold(), that work on collections.

exercises.question: What is a List in Kotlin?
exercises.answer: An ordered collection of elements
exercises.explain: A List is a collection where elements have a specific order and can be accessed by index.

exercises.question: How do you create a List in Kotlin?
exercises.answer: val list = listOf(1, 2, 3)
exercises.explain: listOf() creates a read-only List from the provided elements.

exercises.question: What is the difference between List and Set?
exercises.answer: List is ordered and allows duplicates; Set holds only unique elements
exercises.explain: A List keeps its elements in order, accessible by index, and can contain the same value more than once. A Set stores each value at most once and is not accessed by index.
choices: List is ordered and allows duplicates; Set holds only unique elements
Set keeps duplicates; List removes them

exercises.question: What is a Map in Kotlin?
exercises.answer: A collection of key-value pairs
exercises.explain: A Map stores pairs of keys and values, allowing you to look up values by key.

exercises.question: How do you access an element in a List by index?
exercises.answer: list[0] or list.get(0)
exercises.explain: Both bracket notation and the get() method access list elements by index.

exercises.question: What is an extension function in Kotlin?
exercises.answer: A function added to an existing class without inheritance
exercises.explain: Extension functions let you add new methods to classes, even if you do not control their definition.
choices: A function that extends the program
A function added to an existing class without inheritance

exercises.question: How do you define an extension function on String?
exercises.answer: fun String.exclaim(): String { return this + "!" }
exercises.explain: Extension syntax is fun ReceiverType.functionName() { }. this refers to the receiver object, here the String the function is called on.

exercises.question: What does this refer to in an extension function?
exercises.answer: The object on which the extension function is called
exercises.explain: this is the implicit receiver of the extension function.
choices: The class that defines the extension
The object on which the extension function is called

exercises.question: What does list.filter { it > 5 } do?
exercises.answer: Returns a new list with elements greater than 5
exercises.explain: filter is a built-in extension function that selects elements matching the condition.
choices: Returns a new list with elements greater than 5

exercises.question: What is the purpose of built-in extension functions like map and filter?
exercises.answer: To transform and select elements in collections
exercises.explain: These extension functions enable functional programming patterns for manipulating collections.
choices: To transform and select elements in collections
